notes: West Ham were relegated from the Premier League on 24 May 2026 (club statement) and play in the EFL Championship in 2026/27; the league field keeps the batch's value. Owners reflect the club's ownership page (still the pre-September split); the September 2026 agreement (Křetínský 46%, Sullivan 40%, Smith 11%, others 3%) is recorded as a deal because completion was not yet announced. David Sullivan resigned as joint-chair and director in June 2026; Baroness Brady left as vice-chair in April 2026. Companies House PSCs of WH Holding Ltd: Daniel Kretinsky and David Sullivan (each 25-50%). Financials are WH Holding Ltd's FY to 31 May 2025 (PDF on whufc.com); the club's own release text is rendered by script, so the PDF is cited. Forbes' team page shows $1.125B 'Calculated May 2025' (West Ham are not in the 2026 top 30); Forbes 2024-25 figures: revenue $349M (£277M), operating income $69M (£55M). Stadium owner E20 is named on the operator's page but its public ownership is not stated there. No league titles (honours null). Attendance and social counts not found on a citable page. ownership_summary: West Ham United Football Club Limited is owned through WH Holding Limited. The club's ownership page lists David Sullivan 38.8%, Daniel Křetínský's 1890s holdings a.s. 27.0%, Vanessa Gold for the Gold family trust 25.1%, J Albert 'Tripp' Smith's WHU LLC 8.0% and others 1.1%. In September 2026 Křetínský agreed, through pre-emption on the Gold family's stake, to rise to 46% (Sullivan 40%, Smith 11%, others 3%), displacing a provisional sale of the Gold stake to Amanda Staveley's PCP-led consortium; completion had not been announced by the club at the time of research.
